pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as three to four sessions a week covering strength, stamina and mobility, plus five to fifteen minutes of daily mobility work, and explicitly tied to his own complaint: the rep attributed the week-long hamstring soreness to mobility and connective tissue and said the programme would address it. Response: 'yeah, it sounds really good.' No questions and no probing, which is notable from a prospect who had asked detailed technical questions during discovery about form, weight selection and whether his pain was normal.

Presented as whole foods with an eating window and no calorie tracking, framed around his specific problem of team travel and restaurant dinners — 'when you go out to a restaurant with your team you just look at what fits into that protocol'. Response: 'Check, yes' and then 'Yes, yes' to whether he wanted to make the tweaks. He had already said he was not worried about his nutrition ('I feel like I've been eating normally'), so this pillar was solving a problem he did not think he had, and the acceptance is correspondingly thin.

Delivered as the umbrella: onboarding call, app tracking with chasing if workouts are not logged, video form review, Trevor's personal number, and pre-workout technique teaching aimed directly at his fear — 'before you would even do the first workout, Trevor is going to explain to you how to do all of the exercise correctly, so with the goblet squat, you're not going to feel it for another week after it.' He accepted and gave a commitment when asked ('Can you promise yourself that you're actually going to send him those things?' / 'Yes, of course'). Asked afterwards what stood out most, he could not differentiate: 'no, not really anything specific. I think everything with the program is really good, really complete' — uniform acceptance across all three pillars, which is a weaker buying signal than it sounds.

anchors.raw: Before I was just using like my own body weight, because there's like a calisthenics gym in the park, like, beside my home.
anchors.note: His incumbent solution costs nothing and is a two-minute walk away. He has a real complaint about it — he cannot scale the load down far enough to progress — which is the opening, but the gap between free and $6,000 was never quantified and the alternative was never displaced, only supplemented.

anchors.raw: once I started seeing some content in Instagram mostly with the kettlebells, you know, how the algorithm works, I started seeing a lot of stuff with that. And I saw some videos from Trevor, some workouts that I tried and I think it was really good.
anchors.note: He has already trained successfully from the free content and rated it. The paid offer competes directly with material he is consuming daily at no cost, and the eventual outcome of the call was that he was sent another free video.

anchors.raw: let's say for this month and the next one, I am, I don't have any work. So I don't have anything for the next two months... this is my first year paying the taxes, it's really difficult the taxes here so it was from the beginning a lot higher than I was thinking
anchors.note: The decisive anchor and a hard one: one to two thousand available, two months with no invoicing ahead, and a tax liability of unknown size. He also framed it as a principle rather than a preference — 'even with financing, I think it wouldn't be financially responsible' — which no payment structure reaches.

anchors.raw: because I got contacted by Trevor and he got speaking with me and I was curious to see how it works and how the program works and everything. So I just, because he contacted me, I took the opportunity to have the meeting
anchors.note: The single most important anchor for the rollup rather than for this call. This is an outbound-sourced lead who did not go looking for coaching, and he said so when asked directly why he had taken the meeting if he intended to wait. It corroborates the lead-quality complaint recorded in the setter debrief of 10 July — 'there's a lot of volume for sure, but there's literally low intent... they didn't directly ask for the help'.

anchors.raw: when I went to the store to try out some kettlebells, like the 16 kilos already felt like really, really heavy for me, so I started with a variable weight, which starts at 12
anchors.note: He has bought an adjustable kettlebell, trained with it four or five times in a week and a half, and prefers it to what he was doing. Modality risk is zero and prior commitment is real. Mild but genuine, and it was used well — the rep built the fit argument on his demonstrated follow-through, including quitting a ten-year habit.

unmet_demand.want: An answer on whether a week of hamstring pain after his first goblet squats is normal and whether he should train through it — asked twice, in plain terms, and named as his main worry.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He got a heuristic rather than an assessment: a day or two is normal, a week is too much, it could be form or it could be weight, and 'that's something we definitely have to look into at that point.' The point never came. He left the call with the pain unexplained, a free video to follow and a self-directed product, and no clinician was suggested at any stage.

unmet_demand.want: Individual correction of his kettlebell technique so he can progress the weight safely — the thing he identified himself as what needs cracking.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Individual form review belongs to the one-to-one product he was disqualified from on affordability grounds. The tier he was routed to reviews form through peers and community posts — 'people post their own progression, but also post themselves doing this, where Trevor and other people that are going through the same thing actually help you'. What he needs and what he was sold are not the same deliverable.

unmet_demand.want: A way to begin now and pay when work resumes — he wants to start, has abundant free time in exactly the window he cannot pay in, and the rep made that argument himself.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No deferred-start, deferred-payment or pause mechanism exists. Third-party financing was raised and ruled out because he is Ecuadorian rather than American, and instalments were never offered on the main tier. The only lever available was a cheaper product, not a different timing.

unmet_demand.want: Nutrition that survives half his life on the road with a race team eating restaurant dinners chosen by other people — 'it's more out of my control'.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Addressed in principle — look at what fits the protocol when you eat out — but with no mechanism for the specific constraint, which is that meals are selected communally and at short notice. Probably serviceable by a coach; nothing concrete was offered.
